chromaDefinition: CIELAB C* = hypot(a*, b*), D65, from linearised sRGB. C* is zero on any neutral grey, so the field's near-neutral ink and the one hue separate on it, where a hue ANGLE is undefined at zero chroma.
reading: GRÜN · PG-12 MEASURABILITY — the chroma channel's resolution at the levels in play
scope: PUBLISHABLE per A-G111. The hue-carrying class's C* and the medium/hue ratio are SEALED in the companion file — by A-G117 a seal covers any set from which the sealed quantity is derivable, so publishing the medium's C* requires sealing the hue class's.
whyThisExists: §35 A-G119: PG-12's bound was written before anyone asked what a chroma instrument would resolve, and GELB owes PG-12 the fifth A-G95 field — what observation would make it fail on an otherwise compliant build. That field cannot be written without the channel's resolution.

definitions.medium: disc pixels that are not glow, not any sign, and not a relation carrier — the same comparator PG-11 uses
definitions.chromaQuantum: the C* produced by a +/-1 sRGB code step at a given triple: the raster's own chroma resolution there. Near black it is LARGE relative to the chroma being measured.
definitions.bound: PG-12: medium chroma <= 0.02 x the hue-carrying class's chroma

resolutionReading: the medium's median C* is 2.9116 and one sRGB code step at its own modal triple [6,12,17] moves C* by up to 0.505. So the medium's chroma is 5.77 x the raster's chroma quantum there. A bound of 0.02 x another class's chroma is expressible only if that target sits well ABOVE this quantum; whether it does is in the sealed file, and the comparison is the fifth field's to make.

satisfiability.reading: the bound demands the hue-carrying class reach C* 145.58 while GAP_HUE at FULL strength (alpha 1, rgb 245,166,35) has C* only 74.49. No alpha can exceed the hue's own chroma, and the glow is a low-alpha gradient over near-black, so NO rendering of this hue can satisfy the bound. PG-12 as written cannot be satisfied by any build — the mirror of PG-11, which cannot return a verdict on a compliant one.
satisfiability.metricCaveat: CONDITIONAL ON THE METRIC. PG-12 says 'chroma' without naming a colour space or a reference white. This is CIELAB C* (D65). A different definition — relative saturation, chroma in a cone-opponent space, a ratio against each pixel's own lightness — could change the conclusion, and some would make it satisfiable. That the pin's verdict depends on an unnamed metric is itself an A-G95 gap: the carrier is named (hue, on medium pixels) and the QUANTITY is not.
satisfiability.notAnOpinionOnCompliance: this says the pin cannot be met by any artifact, which A-G116 places outside the seal. It says nothing about this build's reading, which is in the sealed file.

nonNeutralityNote: the stage plate rgb(3, 5, 8) is NOT neutral — its own C* is 1.32, because the three codes differ. So the medium carries a non-zero chroma FLOOR from the plate colour alone, independent of any hue leak, and PG-12's 'never leaks to the ground' cannot mean C* = 0.
